title: Polar to Screen Converter
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Polar Coordinates
Screen Coordinates
Trigonometry
Clock Hands
description: Convert a radius and a clockwise clock angle into pixel coordinates on a 240 by 240 screen, and practice predicting x and y.

learningObjectives: Apply x = cx + r sin(theta) and y = cy - r cos(theta) to find pixel coordinates
Predict the pixel position of a clock-hand tip before it is revealed
Explain why screen y uses a minus sign
prerequisites: Screen coordinates with the origin at the top-left (Chapter 10)

keyQuestions: Why is sine paired with x on a clock face?
Where is the point when theta = 180 degrees?
What happens to x and y when r = 0?
commonMisconceptions: y grows upward on the screen (it grows downward)
Clock angles start at 3 o'clock like math angles (they start at 12 o'clock and go clockwise)
assessmentOpportunities: The student computes (220, 120) for r = 100 at 90 degrees.
The student explains that the minus sign makes points above the center have smaller y.
The student gets at least four of five Predict mode problems within 1 pixel.

controls.label: Show formula
controls.description: Shows both formulas with the current numbers substituted

controls.label: Predict mode
controls.description: Hides the point until the student checks a prediction

controls.label: New point
controls.description: Picks a random radius and angle and turns on Predict mode

controls.label: Check
controls.description: Compares the prediction with the answer (1 pixel tolerance)
